question:
A box contains 4 red, 5 white, and 6 green balls. Three balls are drawn at random without replacement. Find the probability that:

(a) All the balls are of different colours.
(b) At least two balls are white.
(c) All balls are of the same colour.
explanation:
Total: $4+5+6=15$ balls

Number of ways to draw 3 balls: $\binom{15}{3} = 455$

(a) All different colours:
Choose 1 red: 4, 1 white: 5, 1 green: 6 ways.
Total: $4 \times 5 \times 6 = 120$
Probability: $120/455 = 24/91$

(b) At least two white:
(i) Exactly two whites: $\binom{5}{2} \times 10$ (for the third from rest)
$=10 \times 10=100$

(ii) All three whites: $\binom{5}{3} =10$

Sum: $100+10=110$
Probability: $110/455 = 22/91$

(c) All same: All reds: $\binom{4}{3}=4$, All whites: $\binom{5}{3}=10$, All greens: $\binom{6}{3}=20$

Total: $4+10+20=34$
Probability: $34/455 = 2/27$ (approx.)
